title: Pigeon pea Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Pigeon pea Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Pigeon pea nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and phosphorus in kadyos, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Pigeon pea nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your kadyos (pigeon pea) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulfur, zinc, iron, magnesium and boron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But sulfur, zinc, iron and boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which pigeon pea nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a pigeon pea nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest pigeon pea nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in pigeon pea

Lower leaves pale and yellow and the young bush stays light green and thin. Kadyos makes its own nitrogen through root nodules, so pale plants usually mean the nodules are few or not working. You see it most at this stage: three to eight weeks after planting.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in kadyos

In a legume this usually means poor nodulation: no inoculant in a field new to the crop, inoculant killed by sun or heat, very acid soil, waterlogging, hot dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer near the seed, which stops nodules from forming.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency yellows the young leaves first. Iron deficiency yellows between green veins on young leaves. To be sure, dig, do not pull, a few plants 3 to 6 weeks after planting, wash the roots and cut some nodules open. Pink to red inside means they are working, white means not active yet, and brown, grey or mushy means dead.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Feed the young crop with a light sidedress of Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14, following the soil test (Texas AandM).

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, inoculate seed with a cowpea group Rhizobium inoculant at planting and keep it shaded.
Phosphorus deficiency in pigeon pea

There are no clear signs on the leaves: plants are just small and stunted with dark green leaves. Because nothing marks the leaves, the shortage is often missed until the soil is tested. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in kadyos
Acid upland soils and soils low in phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency makes plants pale. Drought also stunts plants, but leaves wilt. To be sure, soil test for phosphorus, or compare with a strip given phosphorus.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Give a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter) every 15 days. For the next crop apply 16 20 0 or Complete 14 14 14 at planting, following the soil test.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, apply phosphorus at planting on poor upland soils.
Potassium deficiency in pigeon pea

The leaf tip turns yellow or brown and the yellow spreads along the edges. The tip then scorches, and early on a yellow band sits between the scorched part and the healthy green. Leaves without symptoms are dark green and plants are stunted. You see it most at this stage: mid growth.
Why potassium deficiency happens in kadyos
Sandy soils and soils cropped for years without potash.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium deficiency yellows between the veins with green veins. To be sure, soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Give a 1 percent potassium chloride spray (10 g Muriate of potash per liter) every week. For the soil, apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash in the planting fertilizer on sandy soils.
Sulfur deficiency in pigeon pea

The new leaves turn pale yellow first, and over time the whole plant becomes evenly yellowish. Unlike nitrogen deficiency, the old leaves are not the first to go. You see it most at this stage: early growth to flowering.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in kadyos
Sandy soils low in organic matter and sulfur free fertilizer for years.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency starts on the older leaves. To be sure, soil and leaf test for sulfur.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency
Give a 0.5 percent calcium sulfate spray (5 g per liter). Gypsum to the soil adds sulfur without nitrogen. Follow the soil test.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use gypsum or a sulfur bearing fertilizer every few seasons.
Zinc deficiency in pigeon pea

Plants are stunted and the leaves narrow and pale green or yellow. Yellow starts between the veins at the tip of the leaflets and spreads until only the midrib stays green. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in kadyos
High pH and calcareous soils, and heavy phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Iron deficiency yellows between the veins but keeps the veins and nearby tissue dark green. To be sure, soil test for zinc and pH, or a leaf test.
What to apply for zinc deficiency
Give a 0.5 percent zinc sulfate spray (5 g per liter) every 15 days, or 10 to 15 kg zinc sulfate per hectare to the soil.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add zinc sulfate to the basal fertilizer on high pH soils.
Iron deficiency in pigeon pea

The spaces between the veins of young leaves turn light green. While the veins and the tissue next to them stay dark green. Older leaves look normal, since the shortage shows in new growth. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early growth.
Why iron deficiency happens in kadyos
High pH, calcareous soils and waterlogged patches.
How to tell it apart
Zinc deficiency narrows the leaves and starts at the leaflet tip. To be sure, soil pH test and a leaf test.
What to apply for iron deficiency
Give a 0.5 percent ferrous sulfate spray (5 g per liter) every week.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid limey, poorly drained spots.
Magnesium deficiency in pigeon pea

Leaves pale slightly between the veins while the veins stay dark green. The pale areas then turn rusty brown or bronze, and narrow streaks of dead tissue form between the veins. Edges of young leaves often roll in. You see it most at this stage: mid growth.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in kadyos
Acid sandy soils and heavy potash.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency starts at leaf tips and edges. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and pH.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency
Give a spray of 2 percent magnesium sulfate (20 g Epsom salt per liter) with 1 percent urea (10 g per liter). Use Dolomite on acid soils as the soil test advises.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils with dolomite.
Boron deficiency in pigeon pea

Upper internodes stay short and the top bunches into a rosette. Leaves near the growing point turn yellow and sometimes red, worst at the tips while the bases stay green. You see it most at this stage: flowering.
Why boron deficiency happens in kadyos
Sandy soils low in organic matter and dry spells.
How to tell it apart
Zinc deficiency also shortens internodes but yellows between the veins. To be sure, leaf or soil test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency
Give a 0.2 percent boron spray (2 g borax per liter) every two weeks.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add compost.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any pigeon pea nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your kadyos needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Pigeon pea nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my kadyos leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: young bushes stay pale and thin, with few pink nodules on the roots. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at sulfur deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in pigeon pea?
items.a: Feed the young crop with a light sidedress of Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14, following the soil test (Texas AandM).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in pigeon pea?
items.a: Give a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter) every 15 days. For the next crop apply 16 20 0 or Complete 14 14 14 at planting, following the soil test.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in pigeon pea?
items.a: Give a 1 percent potassium chloride spray (10 g Muriate of potash per liter) every week. For the soil, apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my kadyos lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the pigeon pea nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
